clue.text: One may connect you with Eton — it helps when travelling

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about and do not stay in their printed order

explanation.surface: A boast that Eton connections smooth the way for a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ETON plus IT HELPS gives TELEPHONIST; 'connect you with Eton' sounds like social networking, but is a switchboard putting a call through.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchboard operator's job is putting callers through to the person or line they want.

clue.text: Bank on value one head put on honesty

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: Banking on someone's worth means valuing their honesty above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is geographical: a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbours like Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reliable and truthful in dealings is exactly the quality of a person others can depend upon.

clue.text: Machine operator gives up merrymaking

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to revel is to make merry

explanation.surface: A factory hand abandons the party to get back to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Machine operator' suggests a worker, but it is the handle or bar that works the machine: REVEL read upwards is LEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivoted bar or handle is pulled or pushed to set mechanical equipment working.

clue.text: Design upset cock bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, something set up or upset is turned bottom to top

parts.note: a cock is a valve or tap, as in stopcock

explanation.surface: Someone's pattern has been disturbed by a cockerel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cock bird' reads as a male bird, but 'cock' here is a tap, as in stopcock, and the bird is separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a decorative design, such as a motif repeated on fabric or wallpaper.

clue.text: One against work with artist's model

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a model is someone who poses

explanation.surface: An artist's model objects to the work being done.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is a person who takes the contrary side and resists a proposal.

clue.text: It purred furiously and entered forcibly

indicators.note: something done furiously is wild and chaotic, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A cat purred angrily and then barged into the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or break in violently, the opposite direction to erupting.

clue.text: Fits guarantor in after arranging church festival

indicators.note: what results after arranging is a new ordering of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone guaranteeing a loan is slotted in after the church event is organised.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' belongs to the fodder, though it reads as a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Transfiguration is a feast day, 6 August, celebrating Christ's appearance in glory on the mountain.

clue.text: Consequences if mica is spilt into food

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go into the following word, which surrounds them
spilt material scatters and lands in a jumble, so these letters lose their order

explanation.surface: Warning of what happens if a mineral gets tipped into someone's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled IF MICA goes inside RATIONS after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramifications are the knock-on results or complications that branch out from an action or decision.

clue.text: Clothing with sleeve in belonging to fellows

parts.note: what is under someone is in their possession or charge

indicators.note: this word says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the arm of a garment is its sleeve

explanation.surface: A garment with sleeves that belongs to some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belonging to' gives the opening piece though it comes last in the clue: what is under someone is in their keeping. The sleeve sits inside the fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclothes such as vests and pants are items of clothing worn beneath the outer layer.

clue.text: Water versus Italian spirit

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as in sports fixtures

explanation.surface: A contest between water and Italian liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquavit is a Scandinavian distilled liquor flavoured with caraway, a type of strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Have relevance to saucy article one included

indicators.note: something included is held within, so one piece goes inside another

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a cheeky magazine piece has any bearing on matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a magazine piece, but it is the grammatical article, which takes the one inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain to something is to concern it or be connected with it.

clue.text: Bury back spotted prisoners

indicators.note: read back means taken from right to left

explanation.surface: A burial behind the lines is noticed by captives.
explanation.definitionFit: Internees are people confined during wartime, held captive without trial.

clue.text: Film fool knocking back punch

indicators.note: knocking something back turns it round, so the pair is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A movie clown downs a glass of fruit punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back punch' suggests drinking, but punch is the definition; ET plus SAP reversed gives PASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste someone is a colloquial verb for hitting them hard, beat or thrash.

clue.text: Iris is not performing for press

indicators.note: 'is not' means the two letters of the word is are absent

explanation.surface: An actress named Iris is off the bill, which matters to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron is to press clothes flat with a heated appliance.

clue.text: Developing within popular family in Gateshead

parts.note: a breed is a line or stock

indicators.note: the head of the word is its opening letter

parts.note: Gateshead is a town on Tyneside

explanation.surface: Claims that a well-liked family in a northern English town is developing too closely.
explanation.walkthrough: The town name is split: 'Gates-head' supplies its own selector, so only its first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbreeding is breeding from closely related stock, so a line keeps developing inside one family.

clue.text: Inclination of Foreign Office to raise height

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it upwards

parts.note: taken as written, then read upwards

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office is inclined to put up its stature.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'to' does double duty as fodder and part of the raising signal; the slope comes last though it is first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A foothill is a low rise at the base of a mountain range, a modest elevation of land.

clue.text: Licensed originator is a man

parts.note: the author of a plan originates it

explanation.surface: The man who started it is the one with the licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authorised has official permission or sanction, just as a licence grants.

clue.text: Criticises one fool with poles carrying piano

indicators.note: what is carrying something holds it inside

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person

explanation.surface: An idiot and some Poles lug a piano around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means the compass points N and S; P slips inside MUG.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn is to challenge or call into question someone's honesty or claims.

clue.text: Divorcee wants meter adjusted to maximum

indicators.note: something adjusted has been altered and set in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A divorcee wants the electricity meter turned right up.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme describes the furthest or utmost degree, as far as something can go.

clue.text: Got redhead to massage back with rough edge

indicators.note: read back means taken from end to start

parts.note: the head of red is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone persuades a ginger-haired person to rub their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' looks like a person but is split to give R, joined to RUB, and the lot is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A burr is the jagged ridge left on metal after cutting or drilling it.

clue.text: Artist dropped radio in it, the fool!

indicators.note: the remains go inside the following word
what is dropped is left out of the word

explanation.surface: Someone let the radio fall into the bath and is scolded as a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiot and fool are close synonyms, both meaning a stupid or foolish person.

clue.text: Two men needing mature sponsorship

parts.note: Pat and Ron are men's names

explanation.surface: A pair of men require mature backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronage is the support or financial backing a patron gives to a person or cause.

clue.text: Starts making duck enclosures

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
a pen is an animal enclosure

explanation.surface: A farmer begins building pens for ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something is to begin it, as a show opens or a meeting commences.

clue.text: Wanting information brought back, takes journalist in

indicators.note: what takes something holds it inside
brought back means read from the end towards the start

explanation.surface: Demanding a story be returned, an editor brings a reporter in.
explanation.walkthrough: The final word 'in' looks like the container signal but is fodder, taken inside along with the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting means lacking or requiring something, the same as needing it.

clue.text: One into fencing off tepee is told to go inside

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words before this phrase

parts.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Someone fencing land off is told to go into the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests putting up fences around the tepee, but the definition means the sword sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is one of the three fencing swords, so its specialist is someone keen on the sport.

clue.text: Starts serving drinks, being a shop assistant

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shop worker begins by pouring drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed to sell goods to customers in a store is a sales clerk or assistant.
